item.title: Miharu Takizakura: Japan's 1,000-Year Weeping Cherry Tree — Guide
item.description: Miharu Takizakura — the ‘Miharu Waterfall Cherry’ — is an estimated 1,000-year-old weeping cherry tree, designated a National Natural Monument and ranked among Japan’s three great cherry trees. Its massive, gnarled trunk supports cascading branches that, in full bloom each April, pour down like a pink waterfall, drawing photographers and pilgrims from across Japan. During the roughly two-week blossom festival, the tree is illuminated after dark, creating an especially dramatic sight against the night sky.
